title: Kummer stratum models identify and detect the geometric scalar mate
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended $\ell$-adic norm topology, and a finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$. For $F=E,\Omega$, put $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ on profinite sets, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and let $C_E\to C_\Omega$ be postcomposition with the continuous inclusion [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. Use internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and the unit-normalized adjunction $C_\Omega\otimes^L_{C_E}-\dashv\operatorname{Res}$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction].

Let $k$ have characteristic $p$ and let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-regular-scheme] with finite reduced strict normal crossings divisor $D=\bigcup_{i\in A}D_i$ [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. Put $W=Y\setminus D$, with open immersion $a:W\hookrightarrow Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $L$ be a finite-rank lisse $C_{E,W}$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Set $C_{F,T}=p_T^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], $L_F=C_{F,W}\otimes_{C_{E,W}}L$, and $T_T=C_{\Omega,T}\otimes^L_{C_{E,T}}-$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. Direct images are those of the ordinary module derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Write $\iota:T_W(L[0])\simeq L_\Omega[0]$ for the scalar-unit-normalized finite-free identification. Define $\Theta=(Ra_{*,C_\Omega}\iota)\circ\beta_{a,L[0]}$, where $\beta$ is the pullback/direct-image counit mate [def-sfb-all-continuous-scalar-mate].

For $I\subseteq A$, let $S_I=(\bigcap_{i\in I}D_i)\setminus\bigcup_{i\notin I}D_i$ with reduced locally closed structure and inclusion $s_I$; the empty intersection is $Y$. Suppose that on every nonempty stratum there are a pro-etale covering family $u_\alpha:S_\alpha\to S_I$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and finite-dimensional continuous $E$-representations $M_\alpha$ of $G_I=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^I$, with finite prime-to-$\ell$ image of $H_I=(\prod_{q\ne p,\ell}\mathbf Z_q)^I$. Put $v_\alpha=s_Iu_\alpha$ and $M_{\alpha,F}(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E M_\alpha)$. Supply isomorphisms $\phi_{\alpha,F}:v_\alpha^*Ra_{*,C_F}(L_F[0])\simeq p_{S_\alpha}^*R\Gamma_{G_I}(M_{\alpha,F})$ in the derived module categories, with the following normalization: after scalar restriction, the direct-image map induced by $L\to\operatorname{Res}L_\Omega$ corresponds under $\phi$ to pullback of the map $R\Gamma_{G_I}(M_{\alpha,E})\to\operatorname{Res}R\Gamma_{G_I}(M_{\alpha,\Omega})$ induced by the actual coefficient unit. Here $R\Gamma$ means ordinary derived internal continuous invariants [def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants]. The isomorphisms are compatible with restriction of the covering family.

Let $\sigma_\alpha:C_\Omega\otimes^L_{C_E}R\Gamma_{G_I}(M_{\alpha,E})\to R\Gamma_{G_I}(M_{\alpha,\Omega})$ be the scalar adjunct of that invariant map. Then $v_\alpha^*\Theta$ is identified with $p_{S_\alpha}^*\sigma_\alpha$ by $\phi$ and the scalar-unit-preserving pullback/tensor comparisons [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. In particular, if every $\sigma_\alpha$ is invertible, then $\beta_{a,L[0]}$ is invertible on $Y$. This is a statement about the actual derived morphisms and restrictions on entire strata, including $I=\varnothing$, with no geometric-stalk conservativity assumption and no constructibility assumption on $Ra_*L_F$.

proof.text:
Use the internal/section normalization theorem to perform the calculation in section-ring modules with the specified derived adjunctions. Put $K=L[0]$, $J=L_\Omega[0]$, $F_R=a_R^*$ and $G_R=Ra_{*,R}$ for $R=E,\Omega$. Write $r$ for scalar restriction, $\eta$ for the scalar unit, and $\epsilon$ for the geometric counit. The ring-change theorem supplies $b:r_WF_\Omega\simeq F_Er_Y$ and $d:r_YG_\Omega\simeq G_Er_W$, compatible with geometric transposition. Define $e=r_W(\iota)\eta_K:K\to r_WJ$. We claim that the scalar transpose of $\Theta$ is the actual unit-induced direct image:
$$d_J\,r_Y(\Theta)\,\eta_{G_EK}=G_E(e).$$
Here is the calculation, with the canonical action identifications understood. Let $\lambda:F_\Omega T_Y\simeq T_WF_E$ be the inverse of the normalized scalar-pullback mate. By definition the geometric transpose of $\Theta$ is $\iota\,T_W(\epsilon_K)\lambda_{G_EK}$. Transpose the left side of the displayed equation geometrically using $b,d$. Its transpose is
$$r_W(\iota)\,r_WT_W(\epsilon_K)\,r_W(\lambda_{G_EK})\,b^{-1}_{T_YG_EK}\,F_E(\eta_{G_EK}).$$
The unit equation for the normalized scalar-pullback mate replaces the last three factors by $\eta_{F_EG_EK}$. Naturality of $\eta$ makes the whole composite $e\epsilon_K$. This is also the geometric transpose of $G_E(e)$, by naturality of the geometric counit. Injectivity of the geometric adjunction bijection proves the claim. The normalization of $\iota$ makes $e$ precisely the actual coefficient unit on $L$.

proof.text: For any $q:S\to Y$, use the scalar-pullback comparison to regard $q^*\Theta$ as a map $T_Sq_E^*G_EK\to q_\Omega^*G_\Omega J$. Its scalar transpose is $q_E^*(d_Jr_Y(\Theta)\eta_{G_EK})$, after the action identifications. Indeed the transpose of a map $z:T_S A\to B$ is $r_S(z)\eta_A$; substituting $q^*\Theta$ and the comparison gives $q_E^*r_Y(\Theta)\,q_E^*\eta_{G_EK}$ because the comparison preserves the scalar unit. Step 1 identifies this with $q_E^*G_E(e)$. The comparison's composition identity ensures that this calculation for $q=v_\alpha=s_Iu_\alpha$ agrees with restriction first to the stratum and then to its covering object.

proof.text: Write $A_\alpha=R\Gamma_{G_I}(M_{\alpha,E})$, $B_\alpha=R\Gamma_{G_I}(M_{\alpha,\Omega})$, and $\rho_\alpha:A_\alpha\to rB_\alpha$ for the map induced by the coefficient unit. Apply step 2 with $q=v_\alpha$. The assumed normalization of $\phi_{\alpha,E},\phi_{\alpha,\Omega}$ says exactly that its scalar transpose becomes $p_{S_\alpha}^*\rho_\alpha$. By definition $\sigma_\alpha$ has transpose $\rho_\alpha$. Apply the same unit-preserving pullback calculation to $p_{S_\alpha}$: the transpose of $p_{S_\alpha}^*\sigma_\alpha$ is $p_{S_\alpha}^*\rho_\alpha$. The scalar adjunction is a bijection on these Hom sets, so the two morphisms are equal. Thus the identification concerns the specified derived morphism itself. No claim that isomorphic source and target objects alone determine the arrow is used.

proof.text: The schemes $S_I$ form a finite locally closed stratification of $Y$. For a point $y$ the unique index is $I(y)=\{i\in A:y\in D_i\}$, proving both disjointness and coverage, and each $S_I$ is open in the closed intersection of its selected components. Discard empty strata and enumerate the remaining finite family. The regularity definition already gives local Noetherianness of $Y$. Finite type over $k$ gives a finite affine cover, hence quasi-compactness, so $Y$ is Noetherian. This verifies the hypotheses of the stratum detection theorem, rather than imposing an extra constructibility hypothesis. Reduced locally closed structures are the actual immersions $s_I$ specified in the statement.

proof.text: If all $\sigma_\alpha$ are invertible, their inverse images under $p_{S_\alpha}^*$ are invertible. Step 3 therefore makes every $v_\alpha^*\Theta$ invertible. Apply the unbounded module clause of Noetherian stratum detection with ring sheaf $C_{\Omega,Y}$ and the coverings supplied in the statement; it gives that $\Theta$ is invertible. The internal/section normalization theorem identifies the ordinary unbounded derived categories and these geometric pullbacks, so the theorem applies to precisely these restrictions. Finally $Ra_{*,C_\Omega}(\iota)$ is invertible, since functors preserve inverses, and $\beta_{a,L[0]}=(Ra_{*,C_\Omega}\iota)^{-1}\Theta$. This proves the conclusion. The empty divisor has the single stratum $S_\varnothing=Y$; when $Y$ is empty the same detection theorem includes the empty family. Neither this argument nor steps 1–3 use boundedness, constructibility of the direct image, or conservativity of geometric stalks.

split_report.summary: Proved the geometric scalar mate is the scalar adjunct of the actual unit-induced direct image by computing its geometric transpose. No statement correction and no new nodes.

tool_uses.why: General adjunction-compatible scalar restriction comparisons, needed to compute the actual unit map; no geometric Kummer computation is replaced.
The normalized unbounded scalar adjunction gives uniqueness from the coefficient-unit transpose without flatness.
Its arbitrary-ring unbounded clause detects the actual morphism on all stratum covers; avoids a geometric-stalk or constructibility assumption.
Unit-preserving scalar pullback comparisons and their composition law are used as generic tools; they do not assume scalar/direct-image commutation.
Identifies internal and section-ring K-flat constructions and the actual geometric derived adjunctions, without any coefficient flatness hypothesis.
